name: initrespawn
description: init respawns a dead console line instead of halting.  The console line's /bin/sh IS init's child, so SIGKILLing it is exactly the 'a line died' event; MARK2 can only reach the screen if a SECOND shell reached a prompt afterwards.  Before the itab rewrite init waited on that one pid and returned when it died, and since init has no parent the kernel halted -- nothing after the kill was typeable.  ECHO_OK: 'MARK2' also appears in a post_command. It discriminates because post_commands are typed only if the machine is still alive: against the pre-respawn init the shell's death halted the machine, so MARK2 was never typed and never echoed. Mutation-verified red on the old init.
